firstShown.explanation: The direct rule is that dirty is true exactly when draft differs from the committed value's canonical decimal text. Input edits draft only; valid commits snap to the nearest legal lattice value, with ties downward. Invalid commits preserve all value and draft data while setting error.
firstShown.mapping: Committed value maps to value; editable text maps to draft; validation status maps to error; mode maps to disabled; dirty maps to draft !== String(value).
firstShown.assumptions: config is available on every call, events are legal per the public contract, and state is only the previously returned opaque state.
firstShown.holds: function holds(input,output){if(!Array.isArray(output))return false;return output.every(function(o){return o&&Object.keys(o).length===5&&typeof o.value==='number'&&typeof o.draft==='string'&&typeof o.dirty==='boolean'&&(o.dirty===(o.draft!==String(o.value)))&&(typeof o.disabled==='boolean')&&(o.error===null||o.error==='invalid')})}
